How it works

One request, four steps, one JSON

Upload the file or a link to it. Poll, or give us a webhook - most hour-long meetings come back in under a minute.

  1. 01

    Send audio or a transcript

    Up to 6 hours per file - m4a, mp3, wav, webm - or text you already have. Add the calendar invite and speakers get their names.

  2. 02

    Transcribe and tell voices apart

    31 languages, switching mid-sentence is fine. Every word keeps its timestamp.

  3. 03

    Read the whole meeting at once

    qx-2 holds 400,000 tokens - about nine hours of talk - so a decision taken at minute 5 and reversed at minute 50 comes out reversed.

  4. 04

    Return what was decided

    Decisions, action items with owner and due date, open questions - each with the seconds it rests on.

API

Three lines from a recording to a list

REST over HTTPS, with small SDKs for JavaScript and Python. Your key is scoped to one project and one region.

curl https://api.quillon.example/v1/meetings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $QUILLON_KEY" \
  -F audio=@weekly-sync.m4a \
  -F extract=decisions,action_items \
  -F webhook=https://you.example/hooks/quillon
{ "id": "mtg_8Kq2", "status": "processing", "eta_seconds": 34 }
import { Quillon } from 'quillon';
import { openAsBlob } from 'node:fs';
const q = new Quillon({ apiKey: process.env.QUILLON_KEY });
const meeting = await q.meetings.create({
  audio: await openAsBlob('weekly-sync.m4a'),
  extract: ['decisions', 'action_items'],
});
const { decisions, actionItems } = await q.meetings.wait(meeting.id);
import os
from quillon import Quillon
q = Quillon(api_key=os.environ["QUILLON_KEY"])
meeting = q.meetings.create(
    audio=open("weekly-sync.m4a", "rb"),
    extract=["decisions", "action_items"],
)
result = q.meetings.wait(meeting.id)

Benchmarks

What we measured, including the misses

Measured on 4 to 6 November 2026 against qx-2. How, in the notes below.

91.4% of labelled decisions found (recall)
96.2% action items with the right owner
0.7 invented items per 100 meetings
820ms / 1,900ms p50 / p95 for a 10k-token transcript

p95 is the one we page on

How we measured

The meetings
1,200 recordings (412 hours) in English, German and Spanish from 38 teams who volunteered them for testing. None was used in training.
The labels
Two people marked every decision and action item in each meeting; a third settled disagreements. They agreed before that on 87% of items.
Counting
A decision counts as found when its meaning matches and its timestamp is within 30 seconds. Invented items have no labelled counterpart and were checked by hand.
Latency
5,000 requests per size from a client in the same region (Frankfurt), on a normal working day. The eval script and per-meeting results are available on request.

Security and data

What happens to your recordings

Meetings hold salaries, customers and people's names. These are the rules we run by - and the ones we do not claim yet.

  • Deleted when the job is doneAudio and transcripts are deleted when processing ends. Results stay 30 days unless you delete them sooner.
  • Not used for trainingWe do not train models on your data. The data processing agreement says so in writing.
  • You pick the regionEU (Frankfurt) or US (Oregon), per project. Nothing moves between them.
  • Encrypted both waysTLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, keys rotated every 90 days.
  • Sub-processors namedListed in the agreement; we tell you 30 days before we add one.
  • Keys per projectRevoke one key without touching the others. Every request is in your audit log for a year.

Deleted0 daysafter processing

What we do not claim yet

We hold no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate today; the first audit is planned for 2027. Our security report and the summary of an external penetration test are available on request.
